_comment: PLUGIN DEFAULT CONFIG: committed, read-only at runtime. Per-user values live in 91__UserConfig__LocalOnly/; each point cloud's LAS link, position and clip box live in the model, one record per cloud, with a backup copy per computer (see ARCHITECTURE.md, Config Layers).

clouds._comment: Several point clouds per model (v0.10.0). maxClouds is the most a model can hold (the engine draws at most 16 at once). Each new cloud takes the first palette colour no other cloud of the model uses: it marks the cloud in the dialog, labels it in the viewport while a tool works on it, and is the colour of its points in the Cloud Colour mode.

overlay.name: Na Point Cloud Viewer
overlay.description: Draws the model's point cloud as a locked visual reference. Not selectable, not snappable, not exported.

render._comment: pointBudget is shared by every cloud on show; pointSizePx, opacityPercent and colourMode ('rgb', 'black' or 'cloud': the cloud's own colour) are each cloud's own look. These defaults are the look a new cloud starts with.

cleanColours._comment: Clean tab, Differences view. Moved points shade from movedSmall to movedMax by how far they moved (up to the largest move allowed); unchanged points keep their colour, blended this share towards unchangedTint.

nativeImage._comment: Render scale = output pixels per logical viewport pixel. movingScale (and at most movingBudgetMax points) while the camera moves or something is dragged; fullScale and the whole budget once still for settleSeconds. movingBudgetMax 0 = no cap.

transform._comment: Move gimbal and Rotate protractor. Snap values are per-user defaults; the user can change them on the Transform tab.

clean._comment: Clean tab. Strength 0..100 maps to the physical values documented in 80__System__Clean/...Settings__.rb (50 = the engine defaults the tests use). Advanced values are millimetres unless a unit says otherwise; a typed value replaces the mapped one until Reset to Defaults.

boxes._comment: Crop and Cut (v0.11.0): boxes captured from the clip box that remove points for good, into a NEW LAS. The Keep box removes every point outside it; each Cut box removes every point inside it. maxCutBoxes is at most the engine's 20. keepColour and cutColour are the box outlines drawn in the model; removed points use render.cleanColours.removed in the Differences view. suffix names the new file: <name>_Cropped_01.las.

noise.label: Remove Noise
noise.summary: Removes stray points that sit apart from every surface: single returns and small floating groups. Dense false surfaces, such as a reflection in a window, are kept. Sparse scatter beside windows is only marked, unless Remove reflection scatter is on. Small real objects (handles, pipes, lamps) are kept.

advanced.label: Isolated point ratio
advanced.hint: A point is removed when its nearest neighbours are this many times further away than the spacing of the surface around it.

advanced.label: Detached group size
advanced.hint: A group cut off from every surface with fewer points than this ...

advanced.label: Detached group extent
advanced.hint: ... and smaller than this is removed.

advanced.label: Group link factor
advanced.hint: Points closer than this many local spacings belong to one group.

advanced.label: Neighbour search radius
advanced.hint: Neighbours are only looked for this far.

advanced.label: Sparse scatter ratio
advanced.hint: Off-surface points this many times sparser than the surfaces around them are marked as reflection scatter.

advanced.label: Remove reflection scatter
advanced.hint: Off: sparse scatter beside windows is only marked (orange in Differences). On: it is removed. Dense false surfaces are never removed.

refine.label: Refine Surfaces
refine.summary: Pulls each point part of the way towards a smooth fit of its own surface nearby, along that surface's normal only, so walls get thinner without being flattened. Corners, reveals, sills, skirtings and steps from 30 mm are kept; points where two surfaces meet are left alone. A surface seen twice by different scan passes is marked, never averaged. Walls are never assumed to be plumb, square or flat.

advanced.label: Largest move
advanced.hint: No point is ever moved further than this.

advanced.label: Fit radius
advanced.hint: The surface under a point is fitted over this radius (at most the analysis cell). Smaller keeps finer detail.

advanced.label: Surface band
advanced.hint: Only points this close to their surface are moved.

advanced.label: Analysis cell
advanced.hint: Each surface is judged over 3 x 3 x 3 cells around a point.

advanced.label: Doubled surface gap
advanced.hint: Two sheets of one surface further apart than this are marked as a possible scan registration error.

advanced.label: Scan pass gap
advanced.hint: With GPS time, a pause this long starts a new scan pass.

advanced.label: Leave doubled surfaces as they are
advanced.hint: On: points on a doubled surface are never moved.

advanced.label: Assumed noise
advanced.hint: Used where the scan's noise cannot be measured nearby.

density.label: Reduce Density
density.summary: Thins the cloud by keeping real measured points only, never averages: about one per patch of plain wall or floor, and more at corners, edges, steps and small objects.

advanced.label: Patch size
advanced.hint: About one point is kept per patch this size on plain surfaces.

advanced.label: Detail factor
advanced.hint: Corners, edges, steps and small objects keep patches this many times finer.

scenes._comment: Scenes tab (v0.9.0). A point cloud scene binds the viewer's settings (point budget, size, opacity, colour, show, clip box) to a SketchUp scene, found by Page#persistent_id. viewTypes tell TrueVision which kind of viewport the scene feeds: a Plan or a Site Plan lays over a plan or site plan viewport (both look straight down, drawn in world X and Z), an Elevation or Section over an elevation looking the same way, and a 3D View is listed for later. A parallel-projection scene exports to scale: pxPerPaperMm pixels per millimetre of paper (12 = TrueVision's Tier03 Detail, about 305 dpi), and the scale preset's pointSizePx is the dot size baked into the image (about 10 to 15 mm in the model, never under 1 px). A custom scale uses round(customPointSizeFactor / denominator), clamped. A perspective scene has no scale: its image width sets the detail.

export._comment: Off-screen render of a scene for TrueVision. Tiles of tileSizePx (the engine renders at most 16384 px a side). An image over maxMegapixels is rendered at a lower pixel density instead, and the report says so.
